- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 3–5%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +5% above recent mean), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.2) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; smooth 3-day moving average of sentiment before adjusting forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >10% from 14-day moving average, adjust forecast toward mean reversion (toward 14-day MA) by 5–10%.
- When sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model misaligns with sentiment direction; align forecast slope with sentiment trend direction.
